### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Langer mesomelic dysplasia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.740)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10853)

**Proposed mechanism:** SHOX (HGNC:10853) —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal development regulation (GO:0060172); Skeletal development regulation (GO:0060172) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004303); SHOX (HGNC:10853) —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal development regulation (GO:0060172); Skeletal development regulation (GO:0060172) —LEADS_TO→ Mesomelic limb shortening (HP:0005741). Haploinsufficiency of SHOX disrupts normal skeletal development, leading to short stature in disease A and mesomelic limb shortening in disease B, reflecting distinct but related phenotypic outcomes of impaired skeletal development.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of distinct causal genes for each disease, or evidence that SHOX variants causing one disease do not impact the pathway disrupted in the other, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs145031916)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SHOX in skeletal development can inform therapeutic strategies for both conditions, potentially involving growth hormone therapy or other interventions aimed at promoting skeletal growth.

#### 2. Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)
